title: Procrastination, Perfectionism, and Self-blame are Modern Symptoms of Primeval Survival Instincts
titleZh: 拖延、完美主义、自责，原来是同一回事
summary:
拖延、完美主义，或是对他人突然断联等常见的自我设障与自我伤害行为，表面看似有害且毫无意义，却可能在进化层面具有某种合理性。临床心理学家兼作家查理·赫里奥特-梅特兰在其新书《心理健康中的受控爆炸》中对此作了系统阐释，指出这类自我设障行为实则是大脑在试图保护我们免受不可预测的伤害，因为大脑的核心任务始终是生存，哪怕代价高昂。因此，想要真正摆脱这些令人困扰的行为模式，理解它们本质上是基于过往经历的生存机制与适应性策略，将有助于减轻自责情绪，从而为我们打破循环创造可能。

来源：Discover；作者：Jenny Lehmann；原文发布时间：2026-01-08 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: Common self-sabotaging and self-harming practices, such as procrastination, perfectionism, or ghosting others, may appear destructive and purposeless, but may actually have a logical evolutionary explanation. Outlined in more detail in Charlie Heriot-Maitland’s new book Controlled Explosions in Mental Health, the clinical psychologist and author explains how self-sabotaging behavior stems from our brain trying to protect us from unpredictable harm, as it’s wired for survival, no matter the cost. To break out of these vexing habits, understanding their origins as survival mechanisms and adaptations to past life experiences may help reduce self-blame and enable us to break the cycle.
paragraphs.contentZh: 拖延、完美主义，或是对他人突然断联等常见的自我设障与自我伤害行为，表面看似有害且毫无意义，却可能在进化层面具有某种合理性。临床心理学家兼作家查理·赫里奥特-梅特兰在其新书《心理健康中的受控爆炸》中对此作了系统阐释，指出这类自我设障行为实则是大脑在试图保护我们免受不可预测的伤害，因为大脑的核心任务始终是生存，哪怕代价高昂。因此，想要真正摆脱这些令人困扰的行为模式，理解它们本质上是基于过往经历的生存机制与适应性策略，将有助于减轻自责情绪，从而为我们打破循环创造可能。

paragraphs.contentEn: Unfortunately, our brain’s main goal is not to make us happy, but to ensure our survival. That means the best-case scenario is for it to exist in a predictable world, without too many surprises, Heriot-Maitland explained in a book announcement. To make a controlled and predictable situation out of unknown (and thus threatening) circumstances, the brain sometimes resorts to questionable behaviors, all in the name of protecting us.
paragraphs.contentZh: 需要明确的是，大脑的首要目标并不是让人感到快乐，而是确保生存。赫里奥特-梅特兰在新书活动中进一步解释到，这意味着对大脑而言，最理想的状态是生活在一个高度可预测、意外尽量少的环境中。为了将未知（因而具有威胁性）的处境转化为可控、可预期的局面，大脑有时会采取一些看似值得商榷的行为，但其根本出发点始终只有一个，保护我们自身。

paragraphs.contentEn: “Our brain would rather we were the arbiter of our own downfall than risk being floored by something external. It would rather we were well-rehearsed in receiving internally created hostility than risk being unprepared for it from others,” he said. Because we are hardwired to spot danger everywhere, not just physical, but also emotional, we operate with a “highly sensitive threat-detection and threat-response system.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 他指出：“相比于被外部事件彻底击垮，大脑更倾向于让我们成为自身失败的主导者。它宁可让我们预先反复演练如何承受自己制造的痛苦，也不愿我们在面对外界冲击时毫无防备。”这是因为人类大脑天生被设定为能随时察觉危险，不仅限于身体层面的威胁，也包括情感层面的创伤，所以我们实际上始终受一套“高度敏感的威胁侦测与应对系统”支配。

paragraphs.contentEn: So, how does self-sabotaging present today, in a world without many physical threats like lurking saber-toothed tigers under the canopy? Most commonly, it shows up as procrastination, perfectionism, and self-criticism. Perfectionism and procrastination are often presented as two sides of the same coin. Both distract our attention from important and potentially threatening tasks, either by hyper-focusing on trivial details or by avoiding a pressing task altogether to sidestep failure. Many are also familiar with elevated self-criticism; by constantly blaming ourselves, we hope to regain a sense of agency.
paragraphs.contentZh: 那么，在一个不再有剑齿虎潜伏于丛林树冠之下等直接生理威胁的世界里，自我设障行为如今是如何表现出来的？最常见的形式包括拖延、完美主义以及自我批评。完美主义与拖延常被视为同一枚硬币的两面。两者都会使我们偏离真正重要且可能带来压力的任务，要么过度纠结于无关紧要的细节，要么彻底回避迫在眉睫的工作，从而避免直面失败。许多人也对不断升级的自我批评并不陌生；通过不断责备自己，人们试图重新获得一种对局面的掌控感。

paragraphs.contentEn: A common result of self-sabotaging behavior is the creation of self-fulfilling prophecies, where negative expectations influence behavior and, ultimately, the outcome of a situation. “If we think we are not very good at something, we may not try our best and then end up performing worse than we would have had we made a different prediction,” Heriot-Maitland explained. “Or if we think someone doesn’t like us, and we avoid them, then our fear of rejection may have stood in the way of creating a relationship.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 自我设障行为的一个常见结果是催生所谓的自证预言，即人们的负面预期会影响自身行为，并最终左右事情的发展结果。赫里奥特-梅特兰解释说：“如果一个人认定自己无法做好某件事，往往就不会尽全力去尝试，结果反而比在作出不同预期时表现更差。再比如，当我们认为某个人不喜欢自己，并因此刻意回避，那么对被拒绝的恐惧本身，可能就已经阻碍了一段关系的建立。”

paragraphs.contentEn: One way of breaking the cycle is to recognize that these destructive behaviors have a protective origin, supported by millions of years of neuronal evolution. “Controlled explosions” are often linked to difficult life experiences from our past, and by repeatedly expressing them, they become a way to shield us from a deeper wound. However, this doesn’t mean we should simply accept self-sabotaging behaviors and move on. Heriot-Maitland instead proposes that, in order to reach the psychological “core,” we need to switch gears and become more compassionate with ourselves, a process that takes time. “We don't want to fight these behaviors, but nor do we want to appease them and let them carry on controlling, dictating, and sabotaging our lives. There are choices we have here.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 打破这一循环的一种方式，是认识到这些看似消极的行为其实源于保护性的本能，并且背后有着数百万年神经进化的支撑。“受控爆炸” 常与个人过往的艰难经历相关；通过反复表现出来，这些行为逐渐演变为一种防御机制，用以保护我们免受更深层的创伤。但这并不意味着我们应该简单地接受这些自我设障行为并听之任之。赫里奥特-梅特兰认为，要想触及心理层面的“核心”，我们需要转变心态，对自己抱以更多理解与善意，这是一个需要时间的过程。他强调：“我们不必与这些行为对抗，但也不能纵容它们继续控制、主导并破坏我们的生活。我们在这里其实是有选择的。”
